summary: This note describes the Madagascar Plate (or Madagascar block), the tectonic plate carrying the island of Madagascar, which was once part of Gondwana and later the Indo-Australian Plate. It covers the plate's rifting history from the Karoo rift system through the separations from Africa, Seychelles and India, the island's four geologic units, and its modern seismic and volcanic activity. It also notes debate over whether the Madagascar Plate should still count as independent, since it largely moves with Africa.
one_line: Overview of the Madagascar Plate's formation, Gondwana breakup and rifting history, geologic units, and modern seismic and volcanic activity.
key_facts: The Madagascar Plate, also called the Madagascar block, is a tectonic plate that holds the island of Madagascar.
Rifting in the Somali Basin began at the end of the Carboniferous, about 300 million years ago, as part of the Karoo rift system.
Gondwana breakup and transform faulting along the Davie Fracture Zone began in the Toarcian, about 182 million years ago, following the eruption of the Bouvet (Karoo) mantle plume.
East Gondwana began to break apart about 115–120 million years ago when India began to move northward.
Between 84–95 million years ago, rifting separated Seychelles and India from Madagascar.
Madagascar separated from Africa about 160 million years ago, according to the note's Rifting section.
The entire island of Madagascar is divided into four tectonic and geologic units: the Antongil block, the Antananarivo block, the Bekily Belt in the south, and the Bemarivo Belt in the far north.
The Antongil Block is characterized by a 3.2 Ga gneiss intruded by granite that has undergone greenschist facies metamorphism.
The Antananarivo Block contains 2.5 Ga gneiss layered with younger granitoids and gabbros and has metamorphosed to granulite facies conditions.
The Itremo sheet was folded in the amalgamation of Madagascar about 700 million years ago.
The Davie Ridge in the Mozambique Channel is a now-extinct transform associated with the first rifting event.
The second separation caused volcanism in southern Madagascar and further south, such as on Marion Island.
Madagascar became entirely isolated from any other continent at the end of the Cretaceous.
The most seismically active area of Madagascar is beneath the Ankaratra Plateau, which experienced magnitude 5.2 and 5.5 earthquakes in 1985 and 1991.
The Comoro Islands to the northwest are recently active and are hypothesized to be related to a hot spot.
Since its formation the Madagascar block has moved roughly in conjunction with Africa, raising questions about whether it should still be considered a separate plate.

entities.name: Madagascar Plate
entities.role: tectonic plate holding the island of Madagascar, also called the Madagascar block

entities.name: Gondwana
entities.role: supercontinent to which the Madagascar block was once attached and where Madagascar was formerly located centrally

entities.name: Indo-Australian Plate
entities.role: plate to which the Madagascar block was later attached

entities.name: Karoo rift system
entities.role: rift system of which the Somali Basin rifting was a part

entities.name: Davie Fracture Zone
entities.role: site of transform faulting during the initiation of Gondwana breakup

entities.name: Bouvet (Karoo) mantle plume
entities.role: mantle plume whose eruption preceded the initiation of Gondwana breakup

entities.name: East Gondwana
entities.role: landmass comprising the Antarctic, Madagascar, Indian, and Australian plates that began separating from the African Plate

entities.name: African Plate
entities.role: plate from which East Gondwana began to separate and with which the Madagascar Plate has moved in conjunction

entities.name: Seychelles
entities.role: landmass separated from Madagascar by rifting 84–95 million years ago

entities.name: India
entities.role: landmass that began moving northward during East Gondwana breakup and was separated from Madagascar by rifting

entities.name: East African Orogen
entities.role: orogen in Madagascar formed in the Neoproterozoic to Cambrian assembly of Gondwana

entities.name: Antongil block
entities.role: one of four tectonic and geologic units of Madagascar, with 3.2 Ga gneiss

entities.name: Antananarivo block
entities.role: one of four tectonic and geologic units of Madagascar, with 2.5 Ga gneiss

entities.name: Bekily Belt
entities.role: geologic unit in the south of Madagascar

entities.name: Bemarivo Belt
entities.role: geologic unit in the far north of Madagascar

entities.name: Dharwar Formation
entities.role: formation in India to which the Antongil block has been linked

entities.name: Itremo Group
entities.role: central Madagascar metasediments from African and Indian continental shelves

entities.name: Davie Ridge
entities.role: extinct transform in the Mozambique Channel, and an extension of the East African Rift Zone off the coast

entities.name: Marion Island
entities.role: island south of Madagascar where volcanism associated with the second rifting event occurred

entities.name: Ankaratra Plateau
entities.role: most seismically active area in Madagascar and site of a major volcanic field

entities.name: Aloatra-Ankay rift
entities.role: seismically active rift north of the Ankaratra Plateau

entities.name: Comoro Islands
entities.role: recently active islands to the northwest, hypothesized to be related to a hot spot
